subject: CDBG Public Service Grant Applications
overview: The committee met with planning department staff and representatives from 11 local service agencies to review funding recommendations for the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program. The committee voted to report the applications out favorably.

items.title: CDBG Program and Funding Overview
items.summary: Director Alicia Hunt and Administrator Ashley Williams explained that the current funding recommendations are estimates based on previous years, as final HUD allocations have not yet been announced. The administration plans to adjust all awards proportionally once final federal funding levels are confirmed.

items.title: Action for Boston Community Development (ABCD)
items.summary: Representatives presented a request for the Mobile Homeless Outreach Team, which provides case management and emergency referrals for unhoused residents in Medford.

items.title: Bread of Life
items.summary: The organization detailed its grocery distribution services and fresh produce provision for food-insecure Medford residents through its Malden facility.

items.title: Communitas
items.summary: The agency discussed its request to support a recreation director for programs serving residents with disabilities, including in-person activities like bowling and track.

items.title: The Community Family
items.summary: The agency outlined its adult day health services in Medford, which provide therapeutic activities and nursing care for individuals with Alzheimer's and other memory impairments.

items.title: Medford Council on Aging
items.summary: Director Pam Kelly requested support for senior home maintenance, motor coach transportation for day trips, and social worker assistance.

items.title: Housing Families
items.summary: The organization described its legal services program, which provides eviction defense and advocacy to prevent homelessness for local families.

items.title: Immigrant Learning Center
items.summary: The center detailed its intensive English language and literacy classes for immigrants and refugees, noting a recent return to in-person instruction.

items.title: Medford Public Schools Afterschool Program
items.summary: The district requested tuition assistance scholarships for working families and discussed the significant waitlists and space constraints facing afterschool programming in the city.

items.title: Mystic Community Market (YMCA)
items.summary: The Mystic Valley YMCA presented on its high-volume food distribution market on Mystic Avenue and its local youth center operations.

items.title: SCM Community Transportation
items.summary: The agency described its door-to-door medical transportation services that connect seniors and residents with disabilities to healthcare providers throughout the region.

items.title: West Medford Community Center
items.summary: Representatives described elder service programs focused on nutrition, fitness, and intergenerational projects aimed at preserving local African-American history.

items.title: Public Comment and Resiliency Hub Concept
items.summary: Following a public comment regarding the lack of local NGO infrastructure, the planning department discussed the concept of a 'resiliency hub' to centralize services and improve disaster response. The committee subsequently voted to report the grant recommendations out favorably.
